Header: e.g. Aspavia armigera Green sucking bug or shield bug

Prevention: Planting of clean and healthy seeds for vigorous rice plants
Proper land preparation (brushing, clearing of plant residues, and ploughing)
Monitoring: Regular visit to the farm (from seedling to harvesting stage)
Rice bugs are found in all rice environments.
They are more common in rain-fed and upland rice and prefer the flowering to milky stages of the rice crop.
Adults are active during the late afternoon and early morning.
Under bright sunlight, they hide in grassy areas.
They are less active during the dry season
Frequent observation of rice tillers especially those with depreciable conditions
Closely look at the panicle especially when the crop is at milky stage
Take actions when signs and symptoms are observed on the plant
Direct Control: Hand picking (which is tedious and time consuming).
This can be carried out throughout the growing cycle whenever the pest occurs
Hand pick adults and at premature stage
Restrictions: II (Moderately hazardous); Apply in the morning when adult bugs are active; 70 mls/gallon of water depending on the level of infestation; Re- entry interval is 24 hours; Pre-harvest interval is 3 weeks; Maximum of 2 applications per season
